mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 2 Series 218i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 2 Series 218i engine replacement typically costs between £1,650 and £4,000 depending on the condition (used, reconditioned, or rebuilt) and the specific engine code. Used engines start from around £950, reconditioned units from £1,650, and fully rebuilt engines with a 12-month warranty from £2,200. Labour for supply and fit adds approximately £800-£1,500 depending on the workshop.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a BMW 2 Series 218i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common early warning sign is a rattling noise from the engine on cold start, which typically disappears as the engine warms up. Other symptoms include a metallic ticking sound, engine hesitation, and in severe cases, the engine management light illuminating with camshaft position errors.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 2 Series 218i?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the vehicle's value and the extent of the damage. For a 218i worth £5,000-£8,000 (typical for 2014-2018 models), a reconditioned engine at £1,650-£2,500 is often worthwhile if you plan to keep the car. For newer G42 models worth £15,000+, replacement is almost always justified. If the car is worth under £5,000, a used engine or repair may be more cost-effective.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 2 Series 218i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical BMW 2 Series 218i engine replacement takes 3-5 working days from order to completion, assuming the engine is in stock. Supply-only orders are usually dispatched within 1-2 working days. Supply and fit through our specialist network typically takes 3-5 days, including delivery, fitting, and ECU calibration.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the 218i and the 220i engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The BMW 218i is powered by a 1.5-litre three-cylinder B38 engine producing 136-140hp, while the 220i uses a 2.0-litre four-cylinder B48 engine producing 181hp. The 220i offers significantly more power and torque, but the 218i is more fuel-efficient and lighter, making it the more economical choice for daily driving.

mainEntity.name: Will a replacement BMW 2 Series 218i engine pass the MoT?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - all engines supplied through EnginesMarket are MoT emissions compliant. Rebuilt and reconditioned engines are tested to ensure they meet the original emissions standards for the vehicle's year. Used engines are selected from low-mileage, well-maintained donors and are checked for emissions compliance before dispatch.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 2 Series 218i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 2 Series 218i arrived in 2014 as the entry-level petrol variant across the 2 Series range, bringing BMW's new modular B38 three-cylinder engine to the Coupe, Convertible, Active Tourer and Gran Tourer body styles. Over its production run, the 218i badge has been powered by a mix of 1.5-litre three-cylinder B38 units and, in some markets, a detuned 2.0-litre B48 four-cylinder.

milestones.description: B38A15A, 1.5L turbo petrol, 136hp (F22 Coupe, F23 Convertible, F45 Active Tourer launch)
B38B15M0, 1.5L turbo petrol, 136hp (F46 Gran Tourer launch)
B38A15M1, 1.5L turbo petrol, 140hp (F45/F46 LCI update, power increase)
B48B20M0, 2.0L turbo petrol, 136hp (selected F22/F23 markets, detuned B48)
B48B20, 2.0L turbo petrol, 154hp (G42 218i introduction, new generation)

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW 2 Series 218i is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 2 Series 218i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 2 Series 218i is powered primarily by the B38 family of 1.5-litre three-cylinder turbo petrol engines, which are generally reliable but have a few well-documented weaknesses. The most significant is timing chain tensioner wear, which affects both B38 and earlier-generation units. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Wear - Why the BMW 2 Series 218i B38 Engine Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The timing chain tensioner can lose hydraulic pressure over time, allowing the chain to slacken. This leads to a characteristic rattling noise on cold start and, if left unaddressed, can cause the chain to jump timing with catastrophic engine damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace tensioner and inspect chain guides
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early (before chain stretch)

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace chain, tensioner, guides, and VANOS units
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if rattling is persistent or mileage >60k

repairOptions.specialistPrice: £2,200-£3,800 (matches Section 4's rebuilt figure for B38 codes)
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if engine has jumped timing or suffered piston/valve contact

problems.recommendation: For a BMW 2 Series 218i with timing chain rattle caught early, a tensioner or chain kit replacement is the most cost-effective solution. However, if the chain has already jumped or the engine has suffered internal damage, a full rebuilt engine with upgraded components and a 12-month warranty is the safer long-term investment.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt B38 BMW 2 Series 218i engine prices

problems.h4: Ignition Coil and Misfire Issues - BMW 2 Series 218i B38 Common Running Problems
problems.rootCause: The ignition coils on the B38 engine can degrade over time, leading to misfires, rough idling, and loss of power under acceleration. This is often exacerbated by the high under-bonnet temperatures in turbocharged applications.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Diagnose misfiring cylinder, replace coil pack
repairOptions.longevity: Effective for single or multiple coil failures

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full set of coils and plugs, preventative
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if mileage >50k or multiple coils have failed

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Comprehensive scan, fuel system check, compression test
repairOptions.longevity: If misfire persists after coil replacement

problems.vehicleValueCheck: As above - for a typical £5,000-£8,000 218i, coil replacement is a minor expense and well worth doing. Only consider full engine replacement if misfire has caused secondary damage (e.g. catalytic converter failure).
problems.recommendation: Ignition coil failure is a routine maintenance item on the B38. Replace faulty coils promptly to avoid catalytic converter damage. If you're experiencing persistent misfires, have a full diagnostic run before assuming the worst.

finalCta.h4: Don't Let Engine Failure Write Off Your BMW 2 Series 218i
finalCta.paragraph: The B38 engine is fundamentally robust, but timing chain and ignition issues can escalate quickly if ignored.
